rose.info: Used for skin care and in cosmetics. The petals have anti-inflammatory properties and are often used in face masks and lotions.
rose.habitat: Cultivated worldwide, especially in temperate regions. Thrives in well-drained soil and sunny locations.

tulsi.info: Used in Ayurveda for its medicinal properties. It is believed to enhance immunity and relieve stress.
tulsi.habitat: Native to the Indian subcontinent, grows in tropical and subtropical climates. Prefers sunny locations and well-drained soil.

aloevera.info: Known for its soothing and healing properties. Often used to treat burns, cuts, and other skin issues.
aloevera.habitat: Native to the Arabian Peninsula, but cultivated worldwide. Thrives in arid and semi-arid regions with well-drained soil.

lavender.info: Used in aromatherapy for relaxation and sleep improvement. The scent is known for its calming effects.
lavender.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in dry, sandy, or gravelly soils and prefers full sun.

mint.info: Commonly used to aid digestion and relieve headaches. Mint leaves can be used in teas and culinary dishes.
mint.habitat: Widely distributed in temperate regions. Prefers moist, fertile soil and partial shade but can tolerate full sun.

chamomile.info: Used to promote relaxation and help with sleep. Chamomile tea is a popular remedy for insomnia and anxiety.
chamomile.habitat: Native to Europe and Western Asia. Grows in well-drained soil with full sun exposure.

dandelion.info: Used as a diuretic and to aid digestion. The leaves, roots, and flowers are used in various herbal remedies.
dandelion.habitat: Native to Eurasia and North America. Thrives in a variety of soil types and can grow in both sunny and shaded areas.

ginger.info: Known for its anti-nausea and anti-inflammatory properties. It is commonly used in cooking and as a remedy for nausea.
ginger.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Grows well in tropical and subtropical climates with rich, well-drained soil and partial shade.

turmeric.info: Contains curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. Often used in cooking and for its health benefits.
turmeric.habitat: Native to tropical South Asia. Prefers warm, humid climates with well-drained, fertile soil.

parsley.info: Rich in vitamins and used for its diuretic properties. Parsley is also a common garnish and has various health benefits.
parsley.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in fertile, well-drained soil with partial shade.

thyme.info: Has antimicrobial properties and is used in cooking and medicine. Thyme is also used in traditional remedies for respiratory conditions.
thyme.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Prefers dry, well-drained soil and full sun exposure.

rosemary.info: Used to improve memory and concentration, and for its antioxidant properties. Rosemary is commonly used in culinary dishes.
rosemary.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Thrives in well-drained soil and full sun.

sage.info: Known for its digestive benefits and antimicrobial properties. Sage is often used in cooking and herbal medicine.
sage.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in dry, sandy soil and full sun.

oregano.info: Contains antioxidants and is used for its anti-inflammatory effects. Oregano is commonly used in Italian cuisine and traditional medicine.
oregano.habitat: Native to Europe, the Mediterranean region, and Western Asia. Prefers dry, well-drained soil and full sun.

coriander.info: Used for its antioxidant and digestive benefits. Coriander seeds are used as a spice, and the leaves are used in salads and dishes.
coriander.habitat: Native to regions spanning from Southern Europe and Northern Africa to Western Asia. Thrives in well-drained soil with full sun.

fennel.info: Known for its digestive benefits and ability to reduce bloating. Fennel seeds are used in cooking and traditional remedies.
fennel.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in well-drained soil and full sun.

jasmine.info: Used in aromatherapy for its calming effects and to reduce stress. Jasmine flowers are also used in perfumes and teas.
jasmine.habitat: Native to tropical and subtropical regions. Prefers well-drained soil and full sun to partial shade.

hibiscus.info: Rich in antioxidants and used to lower blood pressure. Hibiscus tea is a popular beverage known for its tart flavor.
hibiscus.habitat: Native to tropical and subtropical regions. Thrives in warm climates with well-drained soil.

echinacea.info: Boosts the immune system and is used to prevent colds. Echinacea is often used in herbal supplements and teas.
echinacea.habitat: Native to North America. Prefers well-drained soil and full sun.

banana.info: Rich in potassium and dietary fiber. Used as an energy source and for digestive health.
banana.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia, now grown worldwide in tropical climates. Requires warm temperatures and moist, fertile soil.

bilimbi.info: Fruit is sour and used in traditional medicine to lower cholesterol and control hypertension.
bilimbi.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Prefers warm, humid climates and well-drained soil.

cantaloupe.info: Rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. Helps with hydration and immune support.
cantaloupe.habitat: Cultivated in warm regions worldwide. Prefers sandy loam soil and full sunlight.

cassava.info: Staple root crop rich in carbohydrates. Used to make flour, tapioca, and traditional foods.
cassava.habitat: Native to South America, widely cultivated in tropical regions. Grows in poor, sandy soils.

coconut.info: Fruit provides water, milk, oil, and fiber. Used in food, cosmetics, and medicine.
coconut.habitat: Tropical coastal regions worldwide. Requires sandy soil and high humidity.

corn.info: Staple cereal crop rich in carbohydrates. Used as food, livestock feed, and biofuel.
corn.habitat: Native to the Americas, cultivated globally. Grows well in warm climates and fertile soil.

cucumber.info: High in water content, promotes hydration and skin health. Commonly eaten fresh or pickled.
cucumber.habitat: Native to South Asia, cultivated worldwide. Prefers warm climates with moist soil.

curcuma.info: Includes turmeric species, used for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant purposes.
curcuma.habitat: Native to tropical South Asia. Thrives in warm, humid regions with fertile soil.

eggplant.info: Rich in fiber, antioxidants, and vitamins. Used in various cuisines worldwide.
eggplant.habitat: Native to Asia, cultivated globally. Prefers warm climates with well-drained soil.

galangal.info: Used in Asian cuisine and traditional medicine. Believed to improve digestion and reduce inflammation.
galangal.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Thrives in tropical climates with moist, fertile soil.

guava.info: Rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. Used to boost immunity and digestion.
guava.habitat: Native to Central America, now cultivated in tropical regions worldwide. Grows in various soils.

kale.info: Leafy green vegetable high in vitamins A, C, and K. Known as a superfood.
kale.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean. Grows well in cool climates with moist, fertile soil.

longbeans.info: Rich in fiber and protein. Commonly used in Asian stir-fries and salads.
longbeans.habitat: Native to Africa, widely cultivated in Asia. Prefers warm climates with well-drained soil.

mango.info: Tropical fruit rich in vitamins A and C. Known for its sweet flavor and health benefits.
mango.habitat: Native to South Asia. Grows best in tropical and subtropical climates.

melon.info: Includes many varieties like honeydew and muskmelon. Hydrating and rich in vitamins.
melon.habitat: Cultivated worldwide in warm climates. Requires well-drained soil and full sun.

orange.info: Citrus fruit high in vitamin C. Boosts immunity and is used in juices, oils, and cosmetics.
orange.habitat: Native to Asia, cultivated worldwide in subtropical climates.

paddy.info: Rice plant, staple food for over half the world’s population.
paddy.habitat: Native to Asia, cultivated in flooded fields in tropical and subtropical regions.

papaya.info: Rich in vitamin C and digestive enzyme papain. Helps with digestion and skin care.
papaya.habitat: Native to the tropics of the Americas. Thrives in warm, humid regions.

pepper_chili.info: Rich in capsaicin, known for its spicy flavor and metabolic benefits.
pepper_chili.habitat: Native to the Americas, now cultivated globally. Prefers warm climates.

pineapple.info: Tropical fruit rich in vitamin C and bromelain enzyme. Aids digestion and boosts immunity.
pineapple.habitat: Native to South America, cultivated in tropical regions.

pomelo.info: Largest citrus fruit, rich in vitamin C and antioxidants.
pomelo.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Grows in tropical and subtropical climates.

shallot.info: Aromatic bulb with antioxidant and antibacterial properties. Used in cooking and medicine.
shallot.habitat: Native to Central or Southwest Asia, cultivated worldwide.

soybeans.info: Rich in protein and used for soy products like tofu, soy milk, and soy sauce.
soybeans.habitat: Native to East Asia, cultivated worldwide. Prefers warm climates.

spinach.info: Leafy green vegetable rich in iron, vitamins, and antioxidants.
spinach.habitat: Native to Persia, cultivated globally. Prefers cool climates with moist, fertile soil.

sweet_potatoes.info: Rich in fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants. Used as a staple food in many cultures.
sweet_potatoes.habitat: Native to Central and South America. Grows in tropical and subtropical climates.

tobacco.info: Cultivated for its leaves, primarily used for smoking and nicotine extraction.
tobacco.habitat: Native to the Americas, cultivated worldwide in warm climates.

waterapple.info: Tropical fruit with hydrating properties. Sweet and crunchy, used fresh or in salads.
waterapple.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Grows in tropical, humid climates.

watermelon.info: Hydrating fruit rich in lycopene and vitamins. Promotes hydration and heart health.
watermelon.habitat: Native to Africa, cultivated worldwide in warm climates.
